probeMissions: MISSION 1 — the broken-pointer bestiary. `runward init --path <dir> --yes --example` (the green request-triage scaffold), then 32 rows appended to the `## Rule conformance` table of runward/architecture.md, one per branch of evidenceReport, six of them deliberately GREEN so the guards are pinned in both directions. Refused rows: `adr:ADR-9999` (malformed), `file:#` (typed pointer with an empty path), `file:code/src/nope-plain.ts` (unresolvable), `file:../outside-evidence/proof.md` (resolves to a real file in a sibling directory outside the project — the temp root carries no .git/pnpm-workspace.yaml/lerna.json/turbo.json/nx.json, so repoRootAbove finds nothing), `file:/etc/hosts` (absolute), `file:code/src/core` (a directory), `file:code/src/locked.ts` (chmod 000), `file:code/src/shortfile.ts:99` (3 lines, >99 characters), `file:code/src/plain.md#" a "` and `test:code/test/plain.md::" a "` (a quoted anchor that trims to one character), one row per committed-report state for SARIF (unparseable/absent/findings), ESLint (unparseable/absent), CycloneDX (unparseable/ambiguous/absent) and lcov (absent/uncovered), `test:...::"absent test name"`, prose rows citing an empty file and an unreadable file, a rule whose signature is `(a+)+` (the ReDoS screen), and two rows whose rule slug is `probe[end]` and `[start]probe` (the two halves of the `/^\[.*\]$/` placeholder anchor). Green rows: a resolving `file:...#SYMBOL`, `adr:0001`, a signature matched only case-insensitively (`ZEBRAWORD` over content spelling `zebraword`), a signature matched by one of two resolved files, a signature matched through a PATH-TOKEN read, and a prose row citing a file whose content (`nowhitespace`) holds no whitespace at all. Four LOW-impact rule files carrying those signatures are dropped into runward/rules/ (adding rule files produces no corpus divergence), and runward/adr/ADR-0000-template.md is added so an adr: pointer resolved against the wrong id lands on the scaffolded template. Pristine: `check --strict` exit 1, 55 conformance gaps. Builder kept at scratchpad/build-mission.mjs.

MISSION 2 — the adversarial variant of mission 1, which exists for two shapes mission 1 cannot express. (a) runward/adr/ADR-undefined-quirk.md: a real, ratified ADR whose file name begins with the literal string `ADR-undefined`, i.e. what `` `ADR-${p.adrId}` `` interpolates to when adrId is undefined. Without it, dropping the `p.malformed` guard merely changes the message; with it, the malformed pointer RESOLVES and the violation disappears. (b) code/src/binary.md — a path-token evidence file holding a NUL byte and invalid UTF-8, carrying a rule signature, read only through the path-token loop; plus code/src/binary-nows.md, four bytes of invalid UTF-8 with no whitespace. Pristine: exit 1, 56 conformance gaps. Builder at scratchpad/build-mission2.mjs.

MINIMAL MISSIONS — 19 one-fault variants of the green `init --example` scaffold, each planting exactly one bad Evidence cell into a single manifest row so the exit code reads directly as "does the evidence layer still see this". Scenarios: malformed-adr, unreadable-typed (file:code/src/locked.dat — chmod 000, and the extension is deliberately outside PATH_TOKEN so the second loop cannot re-diagnose it), unreadable-prose, blank-symbol, blank-testname, line-count, sarif-unparseable, sarif-absent, eslint-unparseable, eslint-absent, sbom-unparseable, sbom-absent, lcov-absent, testname-missing, directory, bracket-end and bracket-start (each ships a corpus rule file literally named `probe[end].md` / `[start]probe.md` so the row names a KNOWN rule and the pointer is the only fault), plus four honest-mission scenarios that start at exit 0: green-adr, green-nowhitespace, sig-case-clean and sig-some-clean (both reusing the shipped rule security-mcp-server-pinning and its signature `pinn(ed|ing)|sha256|digest`, so no rule file is edited and the corpus stays clean). MISSION mbig — the green scaffold with one prose row citing code/src/big.md, a 560 MiB file of ASCII 'a'. It exists to separate `readFileSync(abs, "utf8")` from `readFileSync(abs, "")`: with the encoding the string conversion throws ERR_STRING_TOO_LONG inside the try and is diagnosed; without it the Buffer comes back intact and the conversion throws later, outside every try, killing the process before any JSON is written.
